Web design Birmingham AL businesses need has changed with the city. Birmingham grew up around blast furnaces; today its biggest engine is a university medical center, and a huge share of local owners either work in health care, sell to it, or serve the people who do. A home health agency in Hoover, a physical therapy clinic near Five Points South, a staffing firm placing nurses, a lab courier, a lunch spot that feeds hospital shifts: each one gets checked on a phone before anyone picks up the phone to call.

Dominion Web Design Pro writes those sites by hand. Maurice Johnson builds each one from Big Sandy in East Texas, shows you a free demo before any invoice, and charges a printed one-time price of $497, $997 or $1,997.

From pig iron to patient care

Sloss Furnaces made pig iron in Birmingham from 1882 until 1971. When it closed, preservationists fought off demolition, the city took over the site, and it became a National Historic Landmark. Now it is a museum of industry with a metal arts program and a concert stage. It is a fair symbol of how the local economy turned over.

The center of gravity today is the University of Alabama at Birmingham. UAB says it has some 28,000 employees across its university and hospital entities, and a 2023 economic impact study found UAB supported or sustained about 107,600 jobs in Alabama in 2022, roughly one in every 20 jobs in the state, with an annual impact of $12.1 billion. Jobs on that scale ripple outward into private practices, home care, medical billing, uniform shops, childcare, apartments and restaurants.

What people check on a health-related Birmingham site

The reader is often worried, busy or on a break between shifts. These are the pages that answer them fastest.

A family choosing home care

They want the counties and towns you cover, the kinds of care you give and do not give, how a first visit works, and a number that answers. Bury any of that and they call the next agency on the list.

A patient picking a practice

Accepted insurance in plain text, hours, parking, which providers see new patients, and how to book. A PDF menu of services nobody can read on a phone does not count.

A nurse or tech looking for shifts

Staffing firms need two front doors: one for the facilities that hire them and one for the workers they place. Each needs its own page with its own next step, not one muddled contact form.

Website design Birmingham AL owners need on both sides of Red Mountain

Birmingham customers describe where they live with a mix of neighborhood names and suburbs. Inside the city there are places like Avondale, Lakeview, Five Points South and Woodlawn, each with its own commercial strip. Lakeview and Avondale have seen new restaurants and shops in recent years, Avondale's 41st Street was picked for one of the city's first Complete Streets projects, and Woodlawn got its first new housing construction in more than 50 years with the Park at Wood Station townhomes.

South of Red Mountain are the communities locals call Over the Mountain: Homewood, Mountain Brook, Vestavia Hills and Hoover. They even have their own newspaper. A pediatric dentist in Vestavia Hills and a salon in Avondale are both "in Birmingham" to an outsider, but their customers search by the name they use at home.

That matters because Google says local results depend mainly on relevance, distance and prominence. If your site never says Homewood, it gives Google little reason to connect you with someone searching from Homewood. The fix is not a footer stuffed with town names. It is a page for each place you really serve, written about that place. Nobody can promise you a ranking, and we do not.

A typical owner, walked through

Picture a nurse who left a hospital job to open a small home care agency serving Hoover and Homewood. She has a state license number, a Facebook page and a phone that rings while she is in a client's living room. Here is how a site for her would come together.

First, the demo

She sends the agency name, the towns she covers and the services she offers. Maurice writes a demo built for that agency, and she sees it before paying a cent. If it is wrong, she says so and nothing is owed.

Then, the pages that do the work

A services page that lists what aides do and what they do not, so families know the difference between companion care and skilled nursing. A page for Hoover and a page for Homewood, each mentioning the parts of town she reaches. An about page that tells her story in her words. A careers page, because in home care the next good aide matters as much as the next client.

Last, the phone problem

She cannot answer during a visit. The site's form emails every lead, and on the Agency package she could add an AI phone agent: setup is included, then the agent is free for 7 days and $297 a month for up to 750 minutes, cancel any time. It is not part of the one-time price, and many owners will never need it.

Alabama website design, beyond Birmingham

Many people searching for Alabama website design or Alabama web design are not tied to one city, and the state gives them good reason to look hard. Coverage of the SBA Office of Advocacy's 2025 profiles puts Alabama at more than 449,000 small businesses, 99.4% of all businesses in the state, employing 46.7% of the private workforce. We write for owners anywhere in the state. Firms that sell to defense and aerospace buyers may want our Huntsville page, which is written for that customer.

The packages are the same everywhere: Starter is $497 for five pages and goes live in 7 to 14 days; Pro is $997 for ten pages, ten researched city pages, local schema and Google Business Profile setup, with an AI chat widget free for 14 days and then $297 a month; Agency is $1,997 for keyword research across your area and a page for every town and service pairing worth having, arriving in waves with the first live inside two weeks. We do not sell page counts. Hosting, maintenance and updates are included while you keep the AI agent, or $49 a month without it. You own the site.

Startup help and business support in Birmingham

Innovation Depot

A startup center that opened in 2007 in a former Sears building downtown, in a facility of about 140,000 square feet, and works with UAB. It is often described as the largest tech incubator in the Southeast.

Greater Birmingham SBDC

Birmingham's Small Business Development Center sits inside Innovation Depot at 1500 1st Avenue North. It is part of the Alabama SBDC Network, hosted by the University of Alabama, which gives no-cost, confidential advising. UAB ran its own center until 2008, so older listings may still point there.

Birmingham Business Alliance

The region's business group runs small business programs aimed at what it calls the "missing middle," firms with 6 to 99 employees, including a 12-week intensive called Supplier Scale. In 2026, with Innovate Alabama, it awarded Match for Impact grants to 16 businesses, each receiving at least $40,000 in professional services.

Small Business Week

The Alliance also holds an annual Small Business Week; the 2026 edition ran May 3 to 9. It is a good place to meet the lenders, advisers and buyers who might later visit your website.

Common questions

How much does website design in Birmingham, AL cost?

Prices around Birmingham run from a do-it-yourself builder's monthly fee to custom agency quotes that only arrive after a sales call. Ours are printed: Starter is $497 for five pages, Pro is $997 for ten pages plus ten city pages, and Agency is $1,997 for keyword research and a page for each town and service worth targeting. All three are one-time prices. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent.

Is there an Alabama website design company that builds the whole site for me?

Plenty of Alabama web design firms will, and so do we, though we are based in East Texas rather than Alabama. Maurice Johnson writes and builds every page himself, sends you a free demo first, and hands over a site you own outright. If being able to sit across a desk from your designer in Alabama matters to you, a local firm is the better fit, and that is a fair choice.

Should a medical practice website collect patient health details in the contact form?

We advise against it. Our contact forms email each lead to you, and email is not where you want diagnoses or insurance numbers sitting. We keep the form to a name, a phone number and a short reason for the visit, add a line asking people not to send medical details, and point patients to your patient portal or phone line for anything private. Ask your own compliance adviser what your practice requires.

Do you work like a Birmingham web development agency or company?

For most small businesses, yes: we plan the pages, write them, design and build the site, set up the contact form, and handle titles, descriptions, sitemap and schema. We are not a development company for custom software, so a patient portal, a scheduling system tied to your records, or an online store is outside our packages. If you need one of those, we will tell you before you buy anything.

Can one website cover Birmingham and the Over the Mountain suburbs?

Yes, as long as each place gets its own honest page. Pro includes ten city pages, each researched and written for that town, so a practice or a home care agency can have separate pages for Homewood, Vestavia Hills, Hoover or Mountain Brook. Agency starts with keyword research across your whole area to decide which towns are worth a page at all.

See your website before you pay for it

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
